name: Fraud Investigation Procedure
description: The end-to-end operational procedure for investigating fraud within FirstUK Bank, owned by the Head of Financial Crime and applicable to the Financial Crime, Risk, Compliance, and Legal departments.

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: The individual responsible for the ownership and oversight of the Fraud Investigation Procedure.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: One of the primary audiences and executors of the fraud investigation procedure.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Team, Risk, Compliance, Legal

name: Risk Department
description: A department involved in the execution and oversight of fraud investigation processes.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Team, Risk, Compliance, Legal

name: Compliance Department
description: A department responsible for ensuring the fraud investigation procedure adheres to regulatory standards.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Team, Risk, Compliance, Legal

name: Legal Department
description: A department providing legal oversight and guidance during the fraud investigation process.
context: Audience | Financial Crime Team, Risk, Compliance, Legal

name: Suspected Fraud Investigation Process
description: A standardized operational procedure designed to investigate suspected fraud cases. The process ensures thorough documentation, an appropriate escalation framework, and a coordinated response with law enforcement agencies.
context: Establish standardized procedures for investigating suspected fraud cases
ensuring thorough documentation, appropriate escalation, and coordinated response with law enforcement

name: Fraud Investigation Framework
description: The overarching operational framework used by FirstUK Bank to categorize and analyze different types of fraud, ranging from account takeovers to internal collusion and AML evasion, including typical loss estimates for each category.
context: FirstUK Bank fraud typically falls into

name: Account Takeover Fraud
description: A fraud category where a fraudster gains unauthorized access to a customer account to transfer funds, with typical losses ranging from £500 to £5,000.
context: Fraudster gains access to customer account, transfers funds

name: Unauthorized Transaction Fraud
description: A fraud category where a customer claims a specific transaction was not authorized, with typical losses between £200 and £10,000.

name: Check Fraud
description: A fraud category involving the deposit of stolen or forged checks, with typical losses ranging from £1,000 to £50,000.

name: Card Fraud
description: A fraud category where a card number is stolen and used for online or retail transactions, typically resulting in losses of £100 to £5,000.
context: Card number stolen, used for online/retail

name: Impersonation Fraud
description: A fraud category involving the opening of a bank account using a false identity, with typical losses between £1,000 and £20,000.
context: Fraudster opens account using false identity

name: Internal Collusion Actor
description: An internal employee who facilitates fraud, representing a high-risk category with typical losses ranging from £5,000 to £500,000.

name: AML and Sanctions Evasion Check
description: A critical compliance gate where a customer deliberately attempts to evade screening processes, potentially leading to losses exceeding £1M.

name: Fraud Detection & Intake Process
description: The initial phase of identifying and reporting fraudulent activity through four primary channels: automated systems, customer reports, internal staff detection, and law enforcement notifications.

name: Fraud Detection Engine
description: An automated system responsible for flagging suspicious transactions with a detection rate of over 97%.
context: Fraud Detection Engine (FDE) flags transaction (97%+ detection rate)

name: Automated Transaction Flagging
description: The step where the Fraud Detection Engine identifies suspicious patterns, such as multiple rapid international transfers, and triggers a system alert.

name: Customer
description: The account holder who reports unauthorized transactions or activity via phone or statement review.
context: Customer calls: "I didn't authorize this transaction"

name: Customer Fraud Reporting
description: The process of a customer notifying the bank of unauthorized account activity or disputing a specific charge on their statement.
context: Customer calls: "I didn't authorize this transaction"

name: Internal Bank Staff
description: Bank employees, including tellers and back-office staff, who identify suspicious activity or discrepancies during reconciliation.

name: Internal Suspicious Activity Detection
description: The internal identification of fraud through staff observation of unusual requests or the discovery of discrepancies during back-office reconciliation.

name: Law Enforcement Agency
description: External authorities, including local police, federal agencies (FBI, OFAC), or international bodies, that notify the bank of compromised accounts.

name: External Authority Notification
description: The intake of fraud information sourced from official police reports, federal investigations, or international law enforcement inquiries.

name: Suspicious Transaction
description: Financial events flagged by the FDE or reported by customers and staff as being unauthorized or unusual.

name: Fraud Allegation Intake Process
description: The end-to-end workflow for handling fraud allegations, encompassing initial reporting, triage based on urgency, and immediate account security actions. The process varies between routine and critical timelines depending on the triage outcome.

name: Initial Report Generation
description: The first stage of the process where a Fraud Report Form is completed. This includes capturing a unique Fraud ID, reporter details, customer account information, transaction details, and the reported fraud type and loss amount.

name: Initial Triage Assessment
description: The evaluation of the reported fraud to determine if it is urgent or standard. Urgent cases require action within 1 hour, while standard investigations are handled within 24 hours.

name: Urgency Determination Gate
description: A branching point that splits the workflow into two paths: 'YES' for urgent scenarios (account takeover, large amounts at risk) leading to immediate action, and 'NO' for standard investigations (disputed posted transactions).

name: Immediate Account Security Actions
description: A set of critical mitigation steps to be performed within the first 5 minutes of an urgent triage. These include freezing accounts, blocking cards, resetting passwords, and notifying the customer.

name: Reporter
description: The individual or entity initiating the fraud report, which can be a Customer, Staff member, System, or Law Enforcement representative.
context: Reporter Category: [Customer / Staff / System / Law Enforcement]

name: Financial Crime Head
description: The senior authority responsible for receiving escalations when a fraud allegation involves a loss amount exceeding £5,000.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime Head if >£5,000

name: High Value Escalation — Financial Crime Head
description: An escalation tier triggered specifically when the alleged loss amount is greater than £5,000, requiring the intervention of the Financial Crime Head.
context: Escalate to Financial Crime Head if >£5,000

name: Fraud Allegation Subject
description: The customer whose account is the subject of the fraud allegation and whose security actions (e.g., password reset, account freeze) are being executed.

name: Alleged Fraudulent Account
description: The specific bank account identified in the report that may be frozen or have its sessions terminated to prevent further financial loss.

name: Questioned Transaction
description: The financial events listed in the fraud report with associated dates and amounts that are being investigated for fraud.
context: Transaction(s) in Question: [List with dates, amounts]

name: Customer Debit/Credit Cards
description: The payment cards associated with the customer that are blocked as part of the immediate security actions to prevent further fraudulent activity.
context: Block customer's debit/credit cards (prevent further fraud)

name: Investigation Procedures
description: The operational workflow for conducting investigations, focusing on the systematic preservation and securing of evidence related to fraudulent activity.

name: Evidence Preservation Step
description: The initial stage of the investigation process involving the collection of transaction records, account statements, communications, system logs, device info, geo-location data, and written statements. Requires evidence to be stored in encrypted or locked files with a minimum 7-year retention period.
context: All evidence secured in locked file (physical) or encrypted (digital)

name: Investigation Team
description: The specialized team responsible for managing and accessing the secured evidence files during the investigation process.

name: Fraudulent Transaction Records
description: The specific financial events being investigated, including screenshots and system data used as evidence.

name: Investigated Customer Account
description: The customer account associated with the fraud investigation, specifically requiring statements from 30 days prior to the fraud date.
context: Account statements (30 days before fraud date)

name: Disputed and Flagged Transaction Analysis Process
description: An operational procedure to assess the legitimacy of disputed or flagged transactions by analyzing transaction details, behavioral patterns, and identifying red flags.

name: Transaction Analysis Step
description: A discrete stage in the fraud investigation process where specific transaction attributes and legitimacy assessments are recorded for each flagged item.
context: Transaction Details: - Transaction ID: [ID] - Date/Time: [Exact timestamp]

name: Transaction Legitimacy Assessment
description: A branching decision gate where the investigator determines if the amount, merchant, timing, device, and geo-location are typical or unusual for the customer.
context: Is amount typical for customer? ☐ Yes ☐ No ☐ Unusual
Is geo-location different from normal? ☐ Yes ☐ No ☐ Impossible

name: Red Flag Identification
description: A critical check to identify high-risk indicators such as velocity, unusual timing, high-risk merchants, geo-impossibility, or departures from habitual patterns.
context: Geo-impossibility (2 transactions on opposite sides of world within minutes)

name: Disputed or Flagged Transaction
description: The specific financial event being analyzed for potential fraud, characterized by ID, amount, type, and merchant details.

name: Customer Interview Procedure
description: A formal procedure to conduct a customer interview within 24 hours of a report to distinguish between legitimate and fraudulent activities. It encompasses authentication, account access, device security, communication, recipient verification, and timeline reconstruction.
context: Timing: Within 24 hours of report (unless law enforcement requests delay)
Scope: Understanding customer's legitimate activities vs. fraudulent

name: Authentication and Authorization Review
description: The stage of the interview where the actor verifies if the customer authorized the specific transaction and identifies the relationship between the customer and the recipient.
context: "Did you authorize this transaction of £[amount] on [date]?"

name: Account Access Assessment
description: A review of the customer's physical card security, usage patterns, and password management to identify potential compromises.
context: "Do you share your PIN/password with anyone?"

name: Device Security Evaluation
description: Investigation into the hardware used for online banking, including the presence of unusual apps or history of device loss/theft.
context: "Do you use the same device (phone/computer) for online banking?"

name: Communication Channel Analysis
description: Checking for the presence of social engineering, phishing emails, or suspicious phone calls prior to the transaction.
context: "Have you received suspicious emails requesting information?"
"Did anyone contact you before this transaction?"

name: Merchant and Recipient Verification
description: Determining the customer's recognition of the merchant and the nature of the initiation of contact.
context: "Did you initiate contact, or did they contact you?"

name: Timeline Reconstruction
description: A detailed chronological walkthrough of the customer's day and location during the transaction to identify discrepancies.
context: "When did you first notice the unauthorized transaction?"

name: Interview Documentation
description: The final administrative step involving recording the date, time, method of interview, and the customer's formal statement.
context: Customer statement taken (audio recorded if possible)

name: Interviewing Officer
description: The bank staff member responsible for conducting the interview and documenting the results, as identified by Name and Title in the documentation section.

name: Law Enforcement
description: External authority that has the power to request a delay in the timing of the customer interview.

name: Interviewee Customer
description: The bank customer who is the subject of the fraud investigation and is required to provide statements and answer a series of verification questions.
context: Understanding customer's legitimate activities vs. fraudulent

name: Fact Confirmation Gate
description: A decision point where the customer either confirms the facts of the transaction or disputes them, which likely triggers different investigation paths.

name: Investigated Transaction
description: The specific financial event of £[amount] on [date] that is the primary subject of the authentication and authorization review.
context: "Did you authorize this transaction of £[amount] on [date]?"
When did you first notice the unauthorized transaction?

name: Fraud Evidence Evaluation Process
description: A systematic procedure to assess the likelihood of fraud by scoring various evidence points and determining the appropriate action based on the total fraud score.

name: Evidence Scoring Stage
description: The process of assigning numerical values to specific evidence markers including customer disputes, geo-impossibility, device mismatch, merchant risk, velocity, and customer history.
context: For Each Piece of Evidence, Score
Fraud Score = Sum of Evidence Points (0–12)

name: Fraud Score Outcome Decision
description: A decision gate where the total Fraud Score (0-12) determines whether the claim is confirmed, likely, possible, unlikely, or not likely, triggering different actions such as refunds or denials.
context: 0 | Fraud Not Likely | Deny fraud claim; educate customer

name: Fraud Confirmation and Remediation
description: The action taken when a fraud score of 7 or higher is achieved, involving the issuance of a refund and the commencement of a formal investigation.

name: Customer Education and Claim Denial
description: The final action taken when a fraud score is between 0 and 3, resulting in the denial of the fraud claim and the provision of educational guidance to the customer.
context: Fraud Unlikely | Likely authorized or error; educate customer
Fraud Not Likely | Deny fraud claim; educate customer

name: Claiming Customer
description: The customer whose transaction is being disputed and who may receive a refund or education based on the fraud assessment.

name: Disputed Transaction
description: The specific financial event being analyzed for fraud markers such as geo-impossibility, velocity, and merchant risk.

name: Merchant and Third-Party Fraud Investigation Process
description: A specialized investigative workflow used when fraud involves an external merchant or recipient. It differentiates between card-based transactions and external account transfers to recover funds or trace illicit activity.

name: Card Transaction Merchant Evidence Collection
description: The process of contacting external merchants to gather transaction proof, verify customer presence, obtain records such as footage/receipts, and analyze the merchant's chargeback history.
context: Request proof customer was present (if card-present)

name: External Account Transfer Investigation
description: The stage of investigation focused on external account transfers, involving the identification of the recipient bank, matching recipient names, screening for sanctions/fraud reports, and checking fund status.
context: Request transaction details (recipient name matches account?)
Track recipient account (is it in sanctions list? Multiple fraud reports?)

name: Fund Availability Decision Gate
description: A branching point based on whether funds remain in the recipient account. If funds are present, an urgent recovery is attempted; if withdrawn, the process pivots to law enforcement tracing.
context: If funds still in recipient account: Attempt to recover (urgent)
If funds withdrawn: Trace withdrawal location (law enforcement)

name: Urgent Fund Recovery Action
description: An urgent action taken to recover funds when it is identified that they are still held within the recipient's account.
context: If funds still in recipient account: Attempt to recover (urgent)

name: Law Enforcement Withdrawal Tracing
description: The process of tracing the location of withdrawn funds in coordination with law enforcement after funds have left the recipient account.
context: If funds withdrawn: Trace withdrawal location (law enforcement)

name: Law Enforcement
description: External authority responsible for assisting in the tracing of withdrawal locations once funds have been removed from a recipient account.

name: Recipient Sanctions Screening
description: A mandatory compliance check performed during external transfer investigations to determine if the recipient account appears on a sanctions list.
context: Track recipient account (is it in sanctions list? Multiple fraud reports?)

name: Fraudulent Card Transaction
description: A card-based financial event suspected of fraud that triggers merchant contact and evidence collection.

name: Fraudulent External Transfer
description: A transfer of funds to an external account that is subject to recipient bank identification and sanctions screening.

name: Forensic Investigation Process
description: A specialized operational procedure triggered for high-loss fraud or suspected cybercrime. It involves detailed technical and financial analysis to identify fraudsters, patterns, and entry points, with an estimated timeline of 2–4 weeks.
context: For High-Loss Fraud or Suspected Cybercrime

name: Forensic Analysis Execution
description: The technical execution phase of the investigation comprising email header analysis, device and network forensics, financial money flow tracing, and database queries to identify linked frauds.

name: Forensic Investigator Engagement
description: The formal process of requesting forensic resources via the Head of Financial Crime and transferring the case file to the internal or external forensics team.
context: Request made to Head of Financial Crime
Case file transferred to external/internal forensics team

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: The authority figure to whom requests for forensic investigator engagement must be made.
context: Request made to Head of Financial Crime

name: Forensics Team
description: The internal or external specialist group responsible for conducting the technical forensic analysis and receiving the case file.
context: Case file transferred to external/internal forensics team

name: Forensic Investigation Trigger
description: A decision gate to determine if a case requires forensic investigation based on whether the fraud is classified as 'Serious/Complex', 'High-Loss', or 'Suspected Cybercrime'.
context: For High-Loss Fraud or Suspected Cybercrime

name: Fraud Investigation Decision and Resolution Process
description: The end-to-end operational workflow for concluding a fraud investigation after all evidence has been gathered. This process focuses on categorizing the outcome of a disputed transaction to determine the final resolution path.

name: Investigation Conclusion Step
description: The discrete action of reviewing all gathered evidence to reach a formal determination on the nature of the fraud claim. This step requires selecting one of five predefined determination categories.

name: Fraud Determination Gate
description: A branching decision point where the investigator categorizes the transaction outcome. The paths include Confirmed Fraud, Disputed Transaction, Authorized, Customer Error, or Incomplete, each leading to different resolution outcomes.
context: DISPUTED TRANSACTION — Ambiguous, but balance of evidence favors customer
CUSTOMER ERROR — System worked correctly; customer misunderstood
INCOMPLETE — Insufficient evidence; close with follow-up conditions

name: Disputed Transaction
description: The specific financial event being analyzed within the investigation process to determine if it was authorized, fraudulent, or a customer error.
context: DISPUTED TRANSACTION — Ambiguous, but balance of evidence favors customer

name: Fraud Resolution and Prevention Process
description: An operational workflow to resolve fraud claims based on fraud type, encompassing refund execution, prevention actions, and customer education. It includes specific timelines for refunds under the Direct Debit Guarantee.

name: Fraud Type Determination
description: A critical branching point where the investigator determines if a case is Confirmed Fraud, a Disputed Transaction, Authorized, or Customer Error, leading to different resolution paths.

name: Disputed Transaction Evidence Review
description: A decision gate for disputed transactions to determine if the balance of evidence favors the customer or is inconclusive, affecting the refund amount and follow-up actions.
context: If Balance of Evidence Favors Customer

name: Fraud Refund Execution
description: The sequence of issuing a full refund including accrued interest, timestamping the decision, and notifying the customer in writing within 10 business days per the Direct Debit Guarantee.
context: Issue full refund to customer account
Refund includes interest (daily rate × days delayed)
Process within 10 business days (Direct Debit Guarantee)

name: Fraud Prevention Implementation
description: A set of security hardening steps following confirmed fraud, including card issuance, password resets, 2FA enablement, and account monitoring.

name: Customer Fraud Education
description: The action of educating the customer on how the fraud occurred or explaining the nature of the transaction (e.g., Direct Debit Guarantee) to prevent future occurrences.
context: Educate customer on how fraud occurred
Educate customer (e.g., "Direct Debit Guarantee protection", "Standing Order", etc.)

name: Compromised Mandate Review
description: A review of active standing orders and direct debits to identify if they have been compromised as part of the prevention phase.
context: Review standing orders / direct debits (may be compromised)

name: Fraud Investigator
description: The actor responsible for determining the fraud type, calculating interest for refunds, and executing prevention actions.
context: Issue full refund to customer account

name: Fraud Claiming Customer
description: The bank customer who is the subject of the fraud investigation and the recipient of refunds or education.
context: Educate customer on how fraud occurred

name: Impacted Customer Account
description: The customer account receiving the refund or being flagged for enhanced monitoring due to fraud.
context: Issue full refund to customer account

name: Compromised Payment Card
description: The specific payment card identified as compromised which must be replaced as a prevention action.

name: Fraudulent Transaction
description: The specific financial event being refunded or disputed.
context: Explain transaction was authorized by customer

name: Fraud Classification & Reporting Process
description: The operational workflow for classifying fraud events and executing internal and external reporting obligations, including timelines for regulatory notifications.

name: Fraud Classification Step
description: The action of categorising a fraud event by type (e.g., Account Takeover, Card Fraud), recording the amount, confirmation status, recovered funds, and current resolution status.
context: Fraud Classification: - Type: [Account Takeover / Card Fraud / Check Fraud / Impersonation / Other]

name: Internal Financial Crime Reporting
description: A monthly reporting activity submitted to the Head of Financial Crime providing summaries of fraud cases, trends, and prevention effectiveness.
context: Financial Crime Report (Internal): - Submitted monthly to Head of Financial Crime
Summary of fraud cases by type

name: SAR Filing Procedure
description: The process of filing a Suspicious Activity Report with the FCA within 30 days if fraud is suspected to involve money laundering or sanctions evasion.
context: Suspicious Activity Report (SAR): - File if fraud suspected involving money laundering/sanctions evasion

name: Data Breach Reporting Procedure
description: The procedure for notifying the FCA within 72 hours and the customer immediately if customer data has been compromised.
context: Data Breach Report (If Applicable): - File if customer data compromised

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: The internal authority responsible for receiving and reviewing the monthly Financial Crime Report.
context: Submitted monthly to Head of Financial Crime

name: Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)
description: The external regulatory body that must be notified of SARs within 30 days and data breaches within 72 hours.

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who must be notified immediately in the event of a data breach.

name: SAR Filing Trigger
description: A decision point to determine if a SAR must be filed based on whether fraud involves money laundering or sanctions evasion.
context: File if fraud suspected involving money laundering/sanctions evasion

name: Data Breach Notification Trigger
description: A decision point to determine if data breach reporting is required based on whether customer data was compromised.

name: Regulatory Reporting Compliance Gate
description: The mandatory checkpoint ensuring that legal reporting obligations (SAR and Data Breach) are met within the specified regulatory timelines.

name: Law Enforcement Coordination Process
description: The operational workflow for determining when to report fraudulent activities to the police. It distinguishes between mandatory and optional reporting triggers based on fraud type, value, and customer requests.

name: Police Reporting Trigger Decision
description: A decision point to determine if a case requires a mandatory police report, an optional report, or no report. Mandatory paths are triggered by high values (>£10,000), organized crime, identity theft, or customer request.

name: Mandatory Police Reporting Action
description: The action of filing a report with law enforcement when specific high-risk or high-value criteria are met, such as confirmed fraud over £10,000 or organized fraud rings.

name: Optional Police Reporting Action
description: The discretionary action of encouraging or filing a police report for fraud between £5,000 and £10,000 or cases involving repeated fraudsters.

name: Bank Systems Team
description: The internal technical team that must coordinate with the reporting actor specifically during the handling of check fraud reports.
context: Check fraud (coordinated with bank systems team)

name: Police
description: The external law enforcement agency that receives fraud reports from the bank.

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who may be the victim of fraud and can trigger a mandatory police report by request.

name: Fraudulent Transaction
description: Transactions identified as fraudulent, categorized by value (e.g., >£10,000 or >£5,000) or type (e.g., check fraud) to determine reporting requirements.
context: Check fraud (coordinated with bank systems team)

name: Police Report Process
description: The end-to-end operational workflow for notifying internal stakeholders, filing a formal report with the police, managing evidence, and following up on a case.

name: Internal Notification Step
description: The initial stage of the process where the Head of Financial Crime and Head of Legal are notified, and the decision to report is formally documented.

name: Police Report Filing Step
description: The action of contacting the local police via non-emergency channels, providing evidence, and securing a police reference number for the case file.

name: Evidence Management Step
description: The phase focused on preserving evidence, maintaining the status of the fraudster's account to allow police monitoring, and coordinating communication and data sharing with law enforcement.
context: Don't disturb suspected fraudster's account (police may monitor)
Coordinate with police on customer communication

name: Police Follow-Up Step
description: The final ongoing stage involving periodic contact with the police for status updates, provision of supplementary evidence, and documentation of all interactions.
context: Periodically contact police for case status

name: Head of Financial Crime
description: A senior internal stakeholder who must be notified when a decision is made to file a police report.

name: Head of Legal
description: A senior internal stakeholder who must be notified when a decision is made to file a police report.

name: Local Police
description: The external law enforcement agency responsible for receiving the report, providing reference numbers, monitoring accounts, and requesting evidence.
context: Coordinate with police on customer communication

name: Decision to Report Gate
description: The point in the process where it is determined whether the circumstances warrant a formal police report, which then triggers the notification and filing steps.

name: Suspected Fraudster's Account
description: The specific customer account associated with suspected fraudulent activity that must not be disturbed to facilitate police monitoring.
context: Don't disturb suspected fraudster's account (police may monitor)

name: Fraud Investigation Case Documentation and Closure Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for documenting and closing a fraud investigation case file. It ensures all necessary evidence, analysis, and approvals are recorded before the case is officially closed.
context: Complete Fraud Investigation Case File Must Contain

name: Case File Compilation
description: The action of aggregating all required documentation into a complete case file, including reports, interview notes, evidence, and analysis.
context: Complete Fraud Investigation Case File Must Contain

name: Investigation Conclusion and Determination
description: The step where the investigator finalizes their findings and makes a formal determination regarding the fraud case.

name: Refund Decision Determination
description: The stage of the process where a decision is made regarding whether a refund is applicable to the customer based on the investigation findings.

name: Case Closure Recording
description: The final recording of the date the case was closed and the full timeline of the investigation from the initial report to closure.
context: Timeline of investigation (from report to closure)

name: Manager or Head of Crime
description: The senior authority responsible for the final sign-off of the fraud investigation case file to ensure it is complete and accurate.

name: Refund Applicability Check
description: A decision point to determine if a refund is applicable based on the investigation outcome.

name: Police Report Necessity Check
description: A check to determine if the nature of the fraud requires the filing and inclusion of a police report reference.

name: Investigated Transactions
description: The specific financial events being analyzed, evidenced via screenshots and statements within the case file.

name: Case Closure Process
description: The end-to-end procedure for closing a fraud investigation case. It defines the mandatory criteria for investigation completion, including evidence analysis, determination, refunds, and manager approval.

name: Evidence Gathering and Analysis
description: The initial step where all relevant evidence is collected and analyzed to support the investigation findings.

name: Fraud Determination
description: The step of making a final determination on the case, categorizing it as fraud, not fraud, or inconclusive.

name: Customer Refund Execution
description: The process of issuing a refund to the customer's account if the investigation determines the transaction was unauthorized.
context: Refund of £[amount] issued to your account on [date]

name: Implementation of Prevention Actions
description: Executing security measures to prevent further fraud, including card replacement, password resets, and enabling security features.

name: Police Report Filing
description: The action of filing a formal report with the police regarding the fraudulent activity where applicable.

name: Case Documentation
description: The final administrative recording and documentation of the case details and findings.

name: Manager Approval for Closure
description: Obtaining formal approval from a manager before the case can be officially closed.

name: Customer Closure Notification
description: Sending a formal letter to the customer detailing the investigation finding, action taken, and recommended prevention steps.
context: We have completed our investigation into the disputed transaction

name: Manager
description: The authority responsible for reviewing the investigation and providing final approval for case closure.

name: FirstUK Bank Financial Crime Team
description: The specialized team responsible for conducting the investigation and communicating the outcome to the customer.
context: Best regards, FirstUK Bank Financial Crime Team

name: Fraud Determination Decision
description: The decision point where the investigator determines if the transaction was fraud, not fraud, or inconclusive, which dictates whether a refund is issued.

name: Disputing Customer
description: The account holder who has disputed a transaction and is the subject of the fraud investigation.

name: Customer Account
description: The account where the disputed transaction occurred and where the refund is issued.
context: Refund of £[amount] issued to your account on [date]

name: Disputed Transaction
description: The specific financial event being investigated for potential fraud.

name: Payment Card Replacement
description: The action of cancelling the compromised card and issuing a new one as a prevention measure.

name: Fraud Prevention Measures Process
description: A comprehensive set of prevention measures categorized by fraud type, including Account Takeover, Card Fraud, Impersonation, and Check Fraud. The process defines specific technical controls and verification requirements to mitigate fraudulent activity.

name: Password Complexity Enforcement
description: A security measure within Account Takeover Prevention requiring the enforcement of password complexity standards.

name: Two-Factor Authentication Implementation
description: The mandatory implementation of 2FA across all customer accounts to prevent account takeover.

name: Login Anomaly Monitoring
description: Continuous monitoring of account login patterns to identify anomalies indicative of account takeover.

name: Customer Phishing Education
description: Educational outreach provided to customers to help them recognize and avoid phishing attempts.

name: Chip and Contactless Card Issuance
description: A card fraud prevention measure restricting card issuance exclusively to chip and contactless technology.

name: Transaction Card Alert Setup
description: Enabling SMS alerts for transactions that exceed a specific monetary threshold (£X) to prevent card fraud.

name: Transaction Velocity Checking
description: Implementation of system checks to limit the maximum number of transactions allowed per day per card.
context: Implement velocity checks (max transactions per day)

name: High-Value Transaction Authentication
description: Requirement for explicit customer authentication when a transaction is flagged as high-value.
context: Require customer authentication for high-value transactions

name: Enhanced KYC Verification
description: A rigorous KYC process used specifically to prevent impersonation fraud.

name: Original ID Document Verification
description: The verification of original identification documents to prevent fraud by impersonation.

name: Duplicate ID Monitoring
description: A check performed to identify if the same identification document is being used across multiple applications/accounts.

name: Suspicious Pattern Flagging
description: The process of identifying and flagging patterns of behavior that suggest impersonation attempts.

name: Positive Pay Implementation
description: A check fraud prevention measure where customers must specify the checks they have issued for the bank to validate.
context: Implement positive pay (customer specifies issued checks)

name: Large Check Additional Verification
description: Mandatory additional verification steps required for the processing of large-value checks.
context: Require additional verification for large checks

name: Check Clearing Time Monitoring
description: The monitoring of the time it takes for checks to clear, where unusual delays are treated as red flags for fraud.
context: Monitor check clearing times (unusual delays = red flag)

name: Customer
description: The bank customer who is the subject of fraud prevention measures and is required to provide authentication or specify issued checks.
context: Require customer authentication for high-value transactions

name: High-Value Transaction Authentication Gate
description: A decision point triggered by high-value transactions requiring customer authentication before the transaction can proceed.
context: Require customer authentication for high-value transactions

name: Check Clearing Delay Red Flag
description: An exception trigger where unusual delays in check clearing are flagged as potential fraud.

name: Fraud Investigation and Resolution Process
description: The end-to-end operational workflow for investigating suspected fraud, managing customer notifications, executing refunds, and implementing preventative measures. It emphasizes confidentiality and a strict 7-year record retention policy for audit trails.
context: Complete investigation; only refund if confirmed/likely fraud
Retain files for 7 years minimum (supports audit trail)
Notify within 24 hours so customer can take protective action

name: Fraud Investigation Step
description: A mandatory thorough investigation phase that must be completed before any refund is processed or a customer is reported as a fraudster.
context: Complete investigation; only refund if confirmed/likely fraud

name: Fraud Case File Retention
description: The requirement to maintain and retain fraud case files for a minimum of 7 years following the closure of the case to ensure a valid audit trail.
context: Delete fraud case file after closure
Retain files for 7 years minimum (supports audit trail)

name: Customer Fraud Notification
description: The act of informing the customer about fraud, which must occur within a 24-hour window to allow the customer to take protective action.
context: Notify within 24 hours so customer can take protective action

name: Fraud Prevention Implementation

name: Fraud Investigation and Approval Process
description: An operational workflow for managing fraud investigations based on the monetary value of the fraud or the nature of the activity (serial/pattern). It defines investigation levels, required approval authorities, and expected resolution timelines.
context: Fraud Amount | Investigation Level | Approval Authority | Timeline

name: Level 1 — Routine Investigation (CSR)
description: The lowest tier of fraud escalation for amounts under £500. This level is handled as a Routine investigation with a 2–3 day timeline.

name: Level 2 — Standard Investigation (Manager)
description: The second tier of fraud escalation for amounts between £500 and £5,000. This is classified as a Standard investigation with a 3–5 day timeline.

name: Level 3 — Enhanced Investigation (Risk Manager)
description: The third tier of fraud escalation for amounts between £5,000 and £50,000. This is classified as an Enhanced investigation with a 5–7 day timeline.

name: Level 4 — Complex Investigation (Head of Crime + Legal)
description: A high-level escalation for fraud amounts exceeding £50,000. This is classified as a Complex investigation requiring joint approval from the Head of Crime and Legal, with a 7–14 day timeline.

name: Level 5 — Specialized Investigation (Head of Crime + Police)
description: The highest level of escalation triggered by serial or pattern-based fraud regardless of specific amount. This is a Specialized investigation requiring Head of Crime and Police involvement, with a timeline of 10+ days.

name: Customer Service Representative
description: The staff member responsible for the approval authority of Routine fraud investigations under £500.

name: Manager
description: The staff member providing approval authority for Standard fraud investigations between £500 and £5,000.

name: Risk Manager
description: The authority responsible for approving Enhanced fraud investigations between £5,000 and £50,000.

name: Head of Crime
description: A senior authority required for the approval of both Complex investigations (>£50,000) and Specialized investigations (Serial/Pattern).

name: Legal Department
description: The department providing joint approval authority with the Head of Crime for Complex fraud investigations over £50,000.

name: Police
description: External authority required for joint approval of Specialized investigations concerning serial or pattern fraud.

name: Fraud Amount and Pattern Assessment
description: A decision gate where the fraud amount and the nature of the fraud (single vs serial/pattern) are evaluated to determine the investigation level, approval authority, and timeline.
